  <request>Fix two PMR compliance checking bugs in parallel: bed L1/L2 window measurement and door L1/L2 WC-side exemption</request>
  <investigated>Regenerated and validated bed_l1l2 visual test references across 5 building plan fixtures. Examined bed_l1l2.py clearance measurement logic and identified windows incorrectly blocking wall detection. Launched isolated agent in worktree to investigate door_l1l2.py WC-side exemption requirements, reviewing room_fill.py integration patterns.</investigated>
  <learned>Bed L1/L2 lateral clearance measures wheelchair space beside beds to the wall structure. Windows are openings in walls (not solid obstacles), so measurements must extend through them to reach the actual wall behind. The sliding rectangle algorithm adjusts measurement position along the bed edge when initial sweep hits non-wall obstacles. Door L1/L2 measures clearance on both sides of inside doors, but WC/bathroom rooms should be exempted from testing (wet rooms have different accessibility requirements).</learned>
  <completed>Bug 1 (bed_l1l2) completed on fix_bed_l1l2 branch (commit 9087a63). Removed window from clearance obstacle classes, implemented _measure_l1_with_wall_slide function to find walls behind openings, added freeda fixture showing regression case (L1 now 11.99 dm to wall vs 11.49 dm to window frame). All 5 test_bed_l1l2 tests passing with regenerated references validating the fix.</completed>
  <next_steps>Waiting for Bug 2 agent completion in fix_door_l1l2 worktree. Agent is implementing WC-side exemption logic in door_l1l2.py to skip clearance testing on door sides facing rooms containing WC fixtures. Expected to reduce failures from 4 to 1 on OPAC73 test fixture by exempting 3 WC-facing door sides.</next_steps>
  <notes>Both bugs relate to architectural feature classification in PMR compliance: windows as openings vs obstacles (Bug 1) and WC rooms as exempted spaces (Bug 2). The parallel worktree approach allows independent bug fixes without branch conflicts. Test references in data/tests/ are gitignored, so validation happens locally without version control.</notes>
</summary>
